metadata.title: KP09 · LLE and ISOMAP
metadata.description: Reasoning-led 2.3.1; editable native teaching deck; global manual mode; no narration.

two-goals-title.name: two-goals-title
two-goals-title.text: Choose neighbors, then decide what to preserve

two-goals-context.name: two-goals-context
two-goals-context.text: Distinguish local reconstruction recipes from graph-path distances; neither is a class label.

two-goals-source.name: two-goals-source
two-goals-source.text: PR · KP09 · 1/12  |  Handout §1,§2  |  Manual Next / Prev

two-goals-bubble.name: two-goals-bubble
two-goals-bubble.text: Follow both branches: what is estimated first and then preserved in lower dimensions?

two-goals-lle.name: two-goals-lle
two-goals-lle.text:
LLE: locally linear embedding
Fix recipes, then embed

two-goals-isomap.name: two-goals-isomap
two-goals-isomap.text:
ISOMAP: isometric mapping
Graph distances, then coordinates

local-recipe-title.name: local-recipe-title
local-recipe-title.text: Reconstruct an observation from its neighbors

local-recipe-context.name: local-recipe-context
local-recipe-context.text: $N_i$ contains neighbor indices of point $i$. Each weight row sums to one; nonneighbors and self have zero weight.

local-recipe-source.name: local-recipe-source
local-recipe-source.text: PR · KP09 · 2/12  |  Handout §3  |  Manual Next / Prev

local-recipe-bubble.name: local-recipe-bubble
local-recipe-bubble.text: Subtract each neighbor from the target and derive a constrained quadratic objective.

local-recipe-difference.name: local-recipe-difference
local-recipe-difference.text:
$A_i=[\mathbf x_i-\mathbf x_j]_{j\in N_i}$
$\mathbf e_i=A_i\mathbf w_i,\quad C_i=A_i^TA_i$

local-recipe-singular.name: local-recipe-singular
local-recipe-singular.text: Singular: solve constrained KKT equations, or declare regularization $C_i+\rho\operatorname{tr}(C_i)I$.

negative-weights-title.name: negative-weights-title
negative-weights-title.text: Can extrapolation use only positive weights?

negative-weights-context.name: negative-weights-context
negative-weights-context.text: Three collinear observations are $x_1=0,x_2=1,x_3=2$. Each uses the other two as neighbors.

negative-weights-source.name: negative-weights-source
negative-weights-source.text: PR · KP09 · 3/12  |  Handout §3  |  Manual Next / Prev

negative-weights-bubble.name: negative-weights-bubble
negative-weights-bubble.text: Reconstruct the left endpoint, then the middle point; distinguish recipes from graph adjacency.

negative-weights-meaning.name: negative-weights-meaning
negative-weights-meaning.text: LLE recipe weights may be negative and asymmetric, unlike the previous unit’s nonnegative symmetric adjacency.

fixed-weights-title.name: fixed-weights-title
fixed-weights-title.text: What stays fixed when coordinates change?

fixed-weights-context.name: fixed-weights-context
fixed-weights-context.text: Observations are rows. Keep the estimated $W$ fixed; row $i$ of $Z$ is its new coordinate.

fixed-weights-source.name: fixed-weights-source
fixed-weights-source.text: PR · KP09 · 4/12  |  Handout §4  |  Manual Next / Prev

fixed-weights-bubble.name: fixed-weights-bubble
fixed-weights-bubble.text: Track fixed recipes, collect reconstruction errors into a matrix, and constrain collapse.

nullspace-title.name: nullspace-title
nullspace-title.text: What if there are two zero modes?

nullspace-context.name: nullspace-context
nullspace-context.text: Here $n=3$; keep $W,M$ and enforce $\mathbf z^T\mathbf1=0$, $\mathbf z^T\mathbf z=1$. Columns of $Q$ span the full complement of constants.

nullspace-source.name: nullspace-source
nullspace-source.text: PR · KP09 · 5/12  |  Handout §4  |  Manual Next / Prev

nullspace-bubble.name: nullspace-bubble
nullspace-bubble.text: Identify the nullspace, then exclude constants explicitly rather than trusting solver column order.

nullspace-project.name: nullspace-project
nullspace-project.text:
$Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-1)}$
$Q^T\mathbf1=0,\quad Q^TQ=I$
$Q^TMQ\mathbf v=\lambda\mathbf v$
$\mathbf z=Q\mathbf v$

path-distance-title.name: path-distance-title
path-distance-title.text: Compare a chord with a neighbor path

path-distance-context.name: path-distance-context
path-distance-context.text: Observations are $(-1,0),(0,1),(1,0)$ with radius $1.5$. ISOMAP uses original-space distance as edge length.

path-distance-source.name: path-distance-source
path-distance-source.text: PR · KP09 · 6/12  |  Handout §5  |  Manual Next / Prev

path-distance-bubble.name: path-distance-bubble
path-distance-bubble.text: Select edges by radius, then sum path lengths; do not substitute unit adjacency weights.

mds-rule-title.name: mds-rule-title
mds-rule-title.text: Turn pairwise distances into coordinate inner products

mds-rule-context.name: mds-rule-context
mds-rule-context.text: Euclidean-realizable distances yield inner products by double-centering. $\Delta^{(2)}$ squares entries; $J$ removes the mean.

mds-rule-source.name: mds-rule-source
mds-rule-source.text: PR · KP09 · 7/12  |  Handout §6  |  Manual Next / Prev

mds-rule-bubble.name: mds-rule-bubble
mds-rule-bubble.text: Double-center to remove individual squared norms, then factor the inner-product matrix into coordinates.

mds-rule-identity.name: mds-rule-identity
mds-rule-identity.text: $\|\mathbf y_i-\mathbf y_j\|^2=\|\mathbf y_i\|^2+\|\mathbf y_j\|^2-2\mathbf y_i^T\mathbf y_j$

mds-rule-approximation.name: mds-rule-approximation
mds-rule-approximation.text:
Largest $q$ positive modes;
fewer than all → approximation

mds-example-title.name: mds-example-title
mds-example-title.text: Can one line reproduce these graph distances?

mds-example-context.name: mds-example-context
mds-example-context.text: Reuse the graph distances. Here $n=3$ and $J=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/3$.

mds-example-source.name: mds-example-source
mds-example-source.text: PR · KP09 · 8/12  |  Handout §6  |  Manual Next / Prev

mds-example-bubble.name: mds-example-bubble
mds-example-bubble.text: Square entries, double-center, keep positive directions, then verify all three distances.

algorithm-title.name: algorithm-title
algorithm-title.text: Which steps can change the final representation?

algorithm-context.name: algorithm-context
algorithm-context.text: Trace a reproducible computation chain for each method and identify numerical and data conditions.

algorithm-source.name: algorithm-source
algorithm-source.text: PR · KP09 · 9/12  |  Handout §7  |  Manual Next / Prev

algorithm-bubble.name: algorithm-bubble
algorithm-bubble.text: Check singular systems, disconnected graphs, and negative eigenvalues against the assumptions of each step.

algorithm-lle.name: algorithm-lle
algorithm-lle.text: LLE: neighbors → constrained recipes (declare regularization) → fix $W$ → solve after excluding constants

algorithm-iso.name: algorithm-iso
algorithm-iso.text: ISOMAP: distance-weighted graph → all-pairs shortest paths → double-centering → positive eigendirections

algorithm-disconnect.name: algorithm-disconnect
algorithm-disconnect.text:
Disconnected → infinite distances
Resolve components or graph design

algorithm-negative.name: algorithm-negative
algorithm-negative.text:
Negative eigenvalues → mismatch
Keeping positive directions is approximate

compare-title.name: compare-title
compare-title.text: Read three methods by what they preserve

compare-context.name: compare-context
compare-context.text: Model choice requires data and task validation. These pairs represent objectives rather than performance rankings.

compare-source.name: compare-source
compare-source.text: PR · KP09 · 10/12  |  Handout §8  |  Manual Next / Prev

compare-bubble.name: compare-bubble
compare-bubble.text: Explain each method through its penalized quantity, then inspect scale, graph, and new-point protocols.

compare-ISOgoal.name: compare-ISOgoal
compare-ISOgoal.text: Graph distances → centered inner products → coordinates

compare-conditions.name: compare-conditions
compare-conditions.text: LLE invariance to translation, rotation, and uniform scale depends on regularization. Dense MDS needs memory. Declare new-point extensions.

new-weights-title.name: new-weights-title
new-weights-title.text: Find recipes for three unevenly spaced points

new-weights-context.name: new-weights-context
new-weights-context.text: New observations are $x_1=0,x_2=2,x_3=5$. Each uses the other two; weights sum to one.

new-weights-source.name: new-weights-source
new-weights-source.text: PR · KP09 · 11/12  |  Handout §9  |  Manual Next / Prev

new-weights-bubble.name: new-weights-bubble
new-weights-bubble.text: Commit all three weight rows, explain any negatives, and verify reconstruction and row sums.

new-distance-title.name: new-distance-title
new-distance-title.text: Embed a new bend using graph distances

new-distance-context.name: new-distance-context
new-distance-context.text: Points are $(0,0),(0,3),(4,3)$ with radius $4.5$. Retain only edges inside the radius, using Euclidean lengths.

new-distance-source.name: new-distance-source
new-distance-source.text: PR · KP09 · 12/12  |  Handout §9  |  Manual Next / Prev

new-distance-bubble.name: new-distance-bubble
new-distance-bubble.text: Find endpoint graph distance and centered one-dimensional coordinates. What changes if the endpoint edge is added?
